Τετάρτη 11 Φεβρουαρίου στις 00:00 | Μέγαρο Μουσικής Αθηνών

The Dimitris Mitropoulos Hall carries the name of Greece's most celebrated conductor — the man who led the New York Philharmonic, who shaped orchestral sound across continents. Tonight, Alexandra Papastefanou plays in his acoustic shadow.

The piano recital at Megaron Mousikis represents a specific kind of musical experience. The Mitropoulos Hall offers the main hall's precision at more intimate scale, seating that places listeners close enough to hear the mechanism of performance — the pedal work, the breathing, the physical effort that becomes invisible in larger spaces.

Papastefanou brings to this room the repertoire and technique that have built her career. Greek pianists navigate a particular challenge: mastering the European tradition while maintaining their own voice within it. The program tonight demonstrates that negotiation — works that reveal training and temperament, technique in service of interpretation.

The audience arrives prepared for serious listening. These are people who know their way around piano repertoire, who can place a interpretation within traditions of approach, who have opinions about phrasing and tempo. Students sit near teachers; subscribers near occasional visitors; everyone united by attention that the piano recital demands.

If you want entertainment between courses, if music should provide background, the piano recital asks the opposite. This is foreground art, performance that assumes your focus, music that rewards the concentration it requires. But if you've been waiting for an evening where the piano speaks and the room listens, where technique serves beauty serves meaning — Megaron's smaller hall tonight offers the encounter.
